1. **Idea:** The animation shows how paying extra on a mortgage compares with putting the same money to another use. An illustrative homeowner, Tessa, has a bill of cash that could go toward the house. The mortgage rate (7.40% a year, before taxes, per the Oct 8, 2026 survey rate) acts as a "bar" that any other use of the money would have to clear.

2. **What changes:** The cash starts beside the house, then moves up onto a gray bar. The bar is labeled "the bar: 7.40% a year, before taxes". Next, a dashed "any other use" cash icon appears beside the bar. Captions are added in turn: "interest no longer charged, not an investment return", then "not tested: how any investment compares, once risk and taxes count". The "ILLUSTRATIVE" and "US only · history, not a forecast" labels stay on screen throughout.

3. **Meaning:** Paying down the mortgage saves 7.40% a year in interest. That saving is a guaranteed avoided cost, not an investment return. Another use of the cash would need to beat that rate, after accounting for risk and taxes, to come out ahead. The animation says it did not test whether any investment actually does.

4. **Advice a viewer might take:** The animation gives no explicit instruction. A viewer might infer that 7.40% is the number to beat before choosing to invest instead of paying extra. They might also infer that this comparison needs risk and taxes added before it can be settled.

5. **Source of the conclusion:** The animation itself suggested this. The "bar" label, the "interest no longer charged, not an investment return" caption, and the "not tested" caption all point that way. It never says "pay extra" or "invest", and the "history, not a forecast" label makes clear it isn't recommending either. The comparison framing comes from the on-screen text, not from my own conclusion.
